text: When Gip said that he wanted the astonishing box, the shopman began to wrap it in a most surprising way. <break time="0.8s" /> He pulled the wrapping paper out of my hat, and then, to my surprise, he drew the string out of his own mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> Next he produced a Disappearing Egg from inside my coat, and he wrapped it up with a Crying Baby, Very Human. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly something moved inside my hat, and a pigeon ran out onto the counter and hurried into a box behind the tiger. <break time="0.8s" /> The shopman shook my hat, and out came two or three eggs, a large marble, a watch, and about half a dozen glass balls. <break time="0.8s" /> After that came crumpled paper, more and more of it, until it rose like a cloud and completely hid the man from view. <break time="0.8s" /> All the while he talked about people who never brush out their hats, and then, quite suddenly, his voice stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> When I asked for my hat and the bill, there was no answer, and behind the counter sat only a white rabbit. <break time="0.8s" /> I thought that if I had known how strange this shop was, I would never have brought my little son into it. <break time="0.8s" /> But when Gip asked the rabbit to do a magic, it slipped through a door, and the shopman came back as if nothing had happened.
